assessment.primary_finding: The 2026 campaign is a shared Vietnamese TikTok-recharge kit. Public-source evidence identifies a likely kit publisher/reseller lead but does not identify the live-domain operator or an individual perpetrator.
assessment.interpretation_rule: Asset or layout reuse can establish technical relatedness; it cannot, without account/log/payment correlation, establish that a repository owner operated a particular domain or payment account.

exact_kit_deployments.why_not_counted: It is not one of the 20 phishing-support submissions in this case inventory.
exact_kit_deployments.interpretation: The public scan requested the same 32 campaign asset hashes and the same Vietnamese title/package/payment presentation. This is a strong kit correlation, not evidence that this domain shared the current origin or payment account.

exact_kit_deployments.why_not_counted: It is a historical public URLScan lead, not one of the 20 phishing-support submissions in this case inventory.
exact_kit_deployments.interpretation: Both historical scans independently show all 32 campaign asset hashes and the same 37-request page bundle. The two scans are retained as corroborating historical kit observations, not as additional case submissions.

public_repository_lead.classification: medium-confidence public kit-publisher/reseller lead; individual identity and live-operator role unproven

independent_classification.interpretation: A third-party phishing classification supports that the published page was suspicious; it does not establish who operated the 20 live domains.

code_and_identity_limits.observed_public_page_behavior: The early page performs a public TikTok-profile lookup and presents a client-side payment/demo flow; it does not call the current campaign backend routes in the captured source.
code_and_identity_limits.current_revision_behavior: The 2026-08-15 revision is a materially different static/demo page and is not treated as the current campaign implementation.
code_and_identity_limits.identity_boundary: The account, repository, public commit metadata, and public email naming convention identify a publisher account, not a verified natural person or live-domain operator.

orvantis_source_page_lead.classification: historical source-page lead; not independently recovered as a live deployment
orvantis_source_page_lead.evidence: The HTML comment in the first seven public repository revisions says the page was saved from this URL.
orvantis_source_page_lead.negative_finding: No independent URLScan page, historical HTML capture, origin address, payment identifier, or server-code link was recovered for nap-xu.orvantis.online.

legacy_kit_lineage.interpretation: Representative historical scan with the same Vietnamese ID-only/no-password wording and ten matching payment/avatar assets; not counted as a current campaign member.
The same old front-end JavaScript hash and matching asset subset predate the QuocTuan repository; this materially weakens any claim that the repository account originated the kit.
This is a historical partial-kit deployment on an address in the same /23 and ASN as the current origin. It is infrastructure continuity evidence, not proof of one customer or operator.
legacy_kit_lineage.registration_context: The current RDAP record is a 2026 re-registration and follows the 2025 URLScan observation; the historical deployment is not dated by that current registration.

unrelated_control.page_title: Different game-recharge portal with Vietnamese corporate footer
unrelated_control.interpretation: The same address served a different portal naming a Vietnamese electronic-sports company. This control demonstrates that the AS/IP is not exclusive to the fake TikTok kit and prevents attribution to the network registrant.

network_control.conclusion: The /23 and ASN support a provider/infrastructure lead only. Subscriber, virtual-host, deployment, and log records are required to attribute the current service.

negative_findings: No current campaign domain, 103.149.86.246 string, live ZaloPay account, or campaign backend route was found in the QuocTuan repository history examined.
No public repository, URLScan, RDAP, or certificate record connects QuocTuan-8386 to ZaloPay app 4982 or the live virtual account.
The shared old JavaScript hash and historical deployments show that the static kit circulated before the QuocTuan account existed; exact assets alone cannot identify the kit author.
No account-level evidence identifies who provisioned the 20 Hostinger domains, configured Cloudflare, or deployed the application on 103.149.86.246.
The unrelated same-IP napgarena.vn control prevents treating the AS149125 registrant as the campaign operator.
method_and_limits: URLScan resource hashes and local SHA-256 hashes were compared byte-for-byte; URLScan pages are historical public observations and may be altered or removed.

The repository comparison checks every captured rc/* asset and every public index.html revision available in the repository at collection time; it does not imply access to private branches, deleted repositories, or server-side code.
Legacy-family observations are intentionally separated from the 20 verified case submissions and should not be added to a blocklist without current validation.

The public email in commit metadata and all credential-like/API-key material were omitted from this derivative; omission does not change the negative finding that no live-domain/payment link was found.
Provider KYC, registrar account records, Cloudflare history, server deployment logs, and payment settlement records remain the decisive next evidence.
